1.title: Make a loop like a 6
1.say: Hold the long part upright in your left hand. Cross the short end over the long part, like a 6.
placements: short loose end → across the front of the long upright part, forming a round open loop hanging below the cross with the end pointing left (in the video: blue rope with red marks, tail to the left and loop to the right)
watch_for: if the loop vanishes when you let go, the short end is likely under the long part instead of over
if there is no round opening below the cross, you crossed too near the tip so slide down
1.check_yourself: It should look like a round ring below with the short end lying across.

2.title: Wrap short end behind long part
2.say: Pinch the bottom loop open with your left hand. Bring the short end behind and around the long part.
placements: short loose end → behind the long upright part then around it to stick out sideways to the right, keeping the round bottom loop open below (in the video: end to the right of the upper cross, bottom loop held in the left hand)
watch_for: if the top looks flat with no twist, the short end likely went in front not behind the long part
if the bottom ring closes up, you pulled the wrap too tight so loosen and reopen it
2.check_yourself: It should look like a twist on top with a loose ring hanging below.

3.title: Thread end through loop and tighten
3.say: Push the short end down through the bottom loop. Pull the long part and short end apart, so the eight tightens.
placements: short loose end → down through the middle of the bottom loop, then long part pulled up and short end pulled down until snug with two stacked rings and a short tail hanging down (in the video: tight eight centred in frame with tail straight down)
watch_for: if pulling makes a single slip loop, the short end missed the bottom loop so rethread it
if the eight looks loose or crooked, both ends were not pulled snug and even
3.check_yourself: It should look like a neat figure eight with a short tail hanging down.
